_source: OSRIC 3.0 Gamemaster Guide §2.13 Magic Items (Tables 2.13.1A–2.13.6.1H). Transcribed verbatim from extracted/gm_guide.txt lines ~17537–19273 and verified against docs/OSRIC_Gamemaster_Guide.md; parsed by scripts/build_magic_items.py. Each sub-table is a metadata wrapper {_table, _title, _die, rows}; each row has roll_range (verbatim), roll [min,max] (00→100 on d100), die, result (verbatim), and value_gp/value_gp_raw where the source gives a gold-piece column. Rows with an embedded 'Roll 1d100' sub-roll keep a structured `subrolls` list. Cursed items table 2.13.10A and full monster/spell detail live outside this range. (AI-assisted) Verify edge cases against docs/ or reference/. OSRIC text © Stuart Marshall & Matthew Finch.

rows.result: Eldritch blast! A catastrophic release of magical energies. This massive energy discharge does 6d10 points of internal damage and 1d10 points of damage to anyone with 10ft of the imbiber. If mixed externally, all persons within 10ft of the epicentre of the blast take 4d6 points of damage, no saving throw allowed.
Poison, causing instant death if mixed internally, no save. External admixtures create a poisonous cloud 10ft in diameter. Anyone within the cloud must save versus poison or die.

A strange brew results and imbiber sickens, losing 1d4 each strength and dexterity for 4d6 rounds, no saving throw. One potion is completely nullified and the other works at 50% strength and duration, determined randomly.
The potions cancel each other out.
One potion is cancelled and the other works at 50% strength and duration, determined randomly.
Both potions work but only at 50% strength and duration.
Successful admixture: both potions work normally.
Extraordinary success: one potion, determined randomly, works at 150% strength and duration while the other is cancelled.

Spectacular success! One of the imbibed potions, determined randomly, has bestowed its effect permanently. Of course, this may not always be a good thing! Consider, for instance, a permanent potion of gaseous form effect.
